newsitem.title: USA: Florida counties to seek court funding amendment.
newsitem.headline: Florida counties to seek court funding amendment.

text.p: Florida Association of Counties will seek a state constitutional amendment requiring the Legislature to fully fund the state court system.

In a meeting Thursday in Fort Lauderdale, association members voted to pursue that avenue rather than sue the state to recoup money counties are forced to pay to support state courts, association spokeswoman Tami Torres said.

Florida's 67 counties pay about 54 percent of the cost of running the courts. In fiscal 1996, they contributed $561 million of the court system's $1.04 billion budget. That has created a hardship for some counties, especially for 14 small counties that are at the legal 10-mill limit for property taxes.

Association members voted against suing the state because the Legislature agreed this year to refund $8.2 million to the counties and to make another $142 million available to them over the next five years to recoup state court costs.
"We made a little bit of headway this session for the first time, so we felt this would be a better way to go than a frontal attack," Hillsborough County Attorney Emeline Acton said.
The Legislature promise to pay all court exepenses when voters agreed to set up the current state court system in 1972, the association said.

The change created a uniform system of county courts for misdemeanor and small claims cases and circuit courts for larger civil disputes and felony cases. Before 1972, each county set up its own court systems.
